newsitem.title: USA: Staples, Depot long brawl with FTC set - arbs.
newsitem.headline: Staples, Depot long brawl with FTC set - arbs.

text.p: The Federal Trade Commission's rejection Monday of the multibillion dollar merger of Office Depot Inc and Staples Inc is the first shot in a long, drawn out battle, arbitrageurs said.
"The companies are adamant about fighting. Both sides said they were willing to go to court, believing the FTC argument is preposterous," said an arb who declined to be named.

"It is going to be long-drawn out process, though there is a chance this a high-stakes game of chicken. There is probably a number of stores (to be divested by the post-merger company) that works for the FTC," he added.

"Maybe this will bring the companies to the bargaining table," the arb added, noting that the four-to-one vote to reject the merger by the commissioners "was much more decisive than we thought. We though it as was a vocal minority against the deal at the FTC."

He said the FTC decision may signal a tougher stance by the commission regarding anti-competitive issues, and if that is the case, the Mattel Inc merger with Tyco Toys Inc is seen as the most vulnerable to greater scrutiny.

A second arbitrageur, who also declined to be named, said, "The rejection was expected by a lot of us in the arbitrage community. We believe there is about a 25 percent chance they can reach a settlement" with the FTC so the merger can proceed.

"We think the government has a very weak case. The FTC is saying they are trying to define the office products market, but people get office product from many sources other than superstores," the arb noted.

"Now we are looking at a time delay. It could take three to four months, but there is still a very good chance the deal will still get done. For arbitrageurs, this makes the transaction less attractive, however it is still a great rate of return," he said.
Terms of the agreement, announced last September, call for Office Depot shareholders to receive 1.14 Staples share for each Office Deport share held.
Immediately after the FTC rejection was announced this morning, Office Depot shares tumbled 4-5/8 to 18, while Staples rose 1-1/16 to 25-5/8.
Trading in both stocks was subsequently halted.
Before the sharp change in the companies' share prices this morning, Staples stock was up 34 percent since the deal was unveiled while Office Depot shares have gained almost 12 percent.
The merged company would have over $10 billion in annual reveues and more than 1100 office supply outlets in the United States and Canada.
